## Welcome to AF 603

This course covers the advanced methods used in fish stock assessments, including population dynamics, data collection, and analytical approaches for sustainable fisheries management.


## Course Modules

### Module 1: Course Introduction  
- Introduction to population dynamics
- Introduction to stock assessment
- Aim of stock assessment
- Definition of key terms

### Module 2: Fish Population Structure
- Key Biological Parameters

  [] Fish population Growth
  [] Fish  recruitment
  [] Fish Mortality

### Module 3: Data Used in Stock Assessment
- Types of data used in stock assessment
- Fishery-Dependent Data
- Fishery-Independent Data
- Data Requirements for Stock Assessments
- Data Quality and Uncertainty
- Sampling design

### Module 4: The Unit Stock
- Distribution  and abundance
- Methods of estimating fish stock abundance

### Module 5: Catchability Selectivity and Multiple Gears
### Module 6: Statistical estimation and model diagnostics
###  Module 7: Biomass and age structured assessment
### Module 8: Per recruit analysis and reference points
### Module 9: Length based assessment for data poor fisheries
### Module 10: Uncertainty and assessment robustness
### Module 11: Management advice projections and strategy evaluation


## Learning Outcomes

By the end of this course, you will be able to:

- Understand the principles of fish population dynamics
- Identify appropriate data collection methods for stock assessments
- Apply statistical methods to analyze fishery data
- Evaluate stock status and provide management recommendations
- Consider ecosystem and social dimensions of fisheries management

## Course Materials

All lecture materials are available in this course website. Each lecture includes:

- Slide presentations (HTML format)
- Key concepts and definitions
- Data examples and case studies
- References and further reading

## Getting Started

Select a module above to begin exploring the course content. Each lecture is self-contained but builds on previous material.
